[ota-hal] OTA-1727 — the card stops cutting the warning off

Three fixed rows, as asked. But I measured the overflow before moving anything,
and it was worse than a layout complaint.

⚠⚠⚠ THERE WERE TWO SILENT CLIPPING SITES, not one. Neither showed an ellipsis,
neither scrolled. The text simply was not there.

  ROW 1 was a `flexDirection: 'row'` with NO `flexWrap`. React Native defaults a
  row to `nowrap`, so every chip past the right edge was cut. Measured on a 320pt
  row (a 360dp phone less the screen, body and stripe insets):

      plain — rarity · dice · durability · equip text ...... 185 of 301 weapons
      coated and reserved ................................. 301 of 301 weapons

  Worst case, the Shockwave Club: 402pt bare, 488pt dressed, into 320.

  ROW 3 was `numberOfLines={1}` — 138 of 301 weapons truncated. What it cut:

      15 weapons never showed that they CANNOT BE COATED
       3 never showed a PERMANENT armour/shield unlock
       3 never showed a flat on-hit rider
       2 never showed the FRIENDLY-FIRE line
       1 never showed that it eventually EXPLODES in your hands
       1 never showed that it pierces armour

⚠⚠ THE FRIENDLY-FIRE ONE IS THE SHARPEST. OTA-1565 added that line with a note
saying this card "is the only warning a player gets before they buy a weapon that
can kill their own dog." Then Row 3 cut it off. The Ember Storm Stave carries
four lines of rules and displayed one:

    Scales with INT · On hit: 1d4 burn/turn for 2 turns · 2d8 to eve…

Everything after that — the splash, and "Power weapon — takes no coating" — was
never on screen.

THE THREE ROWS:

  1  rarity · damage roll (damage type) · durability · on-hit / proc
  2  One-handed | Two-handed · tap to equip / EQUIPPED (main hand)
  3  Scales with STR · resistances · every special property, in full

⚠ FIXED AS LAYOUT, NOT AS TYPE SIZE. You ruled that out by name and the suite
pins it: rowMeta 10, rowHold 10, rowEquippable 10, rowEquipped 10, rowStat 11 —
five assertions, so nothing can be quietly shrunk to buy width later. Moving the
hand and equip chips down to Row 2 is what gives Row 1 its budget back; wrapping
is what guarantees it can never silently cut again. Measured after:

      Row 1 plain ............ 185 of 301 → 0 of 301 over one line
      Row 1 coated+reserved .. 301 of 301 → 5 of 301, and those five WRAP

⚠ "HAND" IS GONE, AND IT WAS THE ODD HALF OF A PAIR. A two-hander announced its
hand COUNT and a one-hander announced only that it went in a hand — two answers
to different questions, so you had to know that "Hand" meant "not the other one".
Both say the count now.

⚠ AND THE HAND LABEL READS THROUGH `resolveDisplayWeapon`, not `findWeaponByName`
— the OTA-705 rule. A fused piece is catalog-absent by design and its name can
collide with an unrelated catalog row, so the name lookup could read a
two-hander's style off a fused vest that merely shares its name. Same defect
OTA-705 fixed for the damage dice, one field over.

⚠ ROW 3 HOISTS THE SCALING STAT. It already led for most weapons, but only by the
accident of `previewWeapon` pushing `Scales with` second and the row filtering out
the first entry. Row order is your requirement, so it belongs to the row.

⚠ AND A GATE CAUGHT ME WRITING THE BUG I SPENT TODAY FIXING. My first
"numberOfLines is gone" assertion used a fixed 120-BYTE window, and
`check:slicepins` refused it: a negative pin measured in bytes goes SILENT as soon
as code grows between the anchor and the forbidden text — it stops checking at
exactly the moment it should scream. Rewritten on `between` + `expectAbsent`,
which bounds the window by the code's own shape and carries a canary proving the
window still looks at the right element.

12 tests, on a REAL render of the screen — the section defaults collapsed, so the
suite expands it and self-checks that the rows are actually there before
asserting anything about them. 19 gates green, complete surface clean.
